analysis.title: Global Fund Performance Monitor: Record October for some funds
key_insights: In October, 46% of Active funds globally outperformed their benchmark, with a median relative return of -0.18%.
Funds with a high Active Share Ratio (>80%) had their best month on record (data since 2015): 65% outperformed by a median +1.16%.
Yield funds also had a record month: 72% outperformed by a median +1.77%.
Value funds outperformed (66% hit rate, median +0.87%) while Growth funds lagged (36% hit rate, median -0.42%).
BofA names interest rates, market breadth and sentiment toward AI-related global themes as the recent drivers of relative performance.

Yield funds' largest overweights are GSK, Sanofi, Targa Resources, TotalEnergies, DT Midstream, Johnson & Johnson and Taylor Wimpey. Their largest underweights are NVIDIA, Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, HSBC and ASML.

High ASR (>80%) funds' largest overweights are TSMC, Edenred, SPIE, Games Workshop, Weir, SpaceX and CATL. Their largest underweights are Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta and Tesla.

By region, EAFE funds outperformed in October (median +0.17%, 64% hit rate). Global DM+EM (-0.34%), Global DM (-0.37%), USA (-0.02%), Europe (-0.13%), Japan (-0.31%), Asia Pac ex-Japan (-0.30%) and EM (-0.55%) funds underperformed.

Mid cap funds outperformed by a median 0.32% (64% hit rate) and small cap funds by 0.31%. Large cap funds underperformed by 0.13%. Small cap YTD median relative return is +4.44%, but only 5 funds are in the group.
Passive and Index funds underperformed by a median 0.08% in October (29% hit rate). Active funds underperformed by 0.18% (46% hit rate).
Among turnover groups, High turnover funds lagged most (-0.63%, 21% hit rate), followed by Medium (-0.57%). Very Low turnover funds lost 0.06%.
Funds with 0-35 holdings outperformed by a median 0.12% (53% hit rate). Funds with 36-75 holdings underperformed by 0.15%.
Over longer horizons, the high-ASR group's median relative return is -2.03% YTD, -3.76% over 2 years and -4.51% over 3 years annualized, so October's record does not change the multi-year deficit.
The universe covers 2,633 long-only equity funds with $21.6tn in FUM and 573 unique benchmarks.
risk_factors: Active fund underperformance relative to benchmark persists over long horizons: median relative return is -1.34% YTD and -2.23% annualized over 2 years.
Large dispersion in high ASR funds: the 1-month spread between top and bottom quartile is 4.68%, and 12m spread is 12.50%.
charts_described: Chart 1 plots the 1-month and 12-month hit rate (share of active funds outperforming benchmark) since Jan-15, with the latest 1-month reading at 46% for Active funds.
Chart 4 shows USA funds are 38% of the fund universe (1008 funds, $13,751 bn).
vol_and_positioning: High ASR (>80%) funds are overweight TSMC, Edenred, SPIE, Games Workshop, Weir, SpaceX and CATL, and underweight Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta and Tesla.
Yield funds are overweight GSK, Sanofi, Targa Resources, TotalEnergies, DT Midstream, Johnson & Johnson and Taylor Wimpey, and underweight NVIDIA, Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, HSBC and ASML.
Both the record-performing high ASR group and Yield funds are underweight the US mega-cap tech names (Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon).
The share of all funds outperforming their benchmark is 40% over 1 month, 30% YTD, 33% over 12 months and 23% over 2 years.
